statement: A 555 timer wired as a nonretriggerable one-shot produces an output pulse whose width is set by one external resistor and capacitor: tW = 1.1*R1*C1. Add a 0.01 uF decoupling capacitor from CONT (pin 5) to ground to keep noise off the trigger/threshold levels.
condition: 555 in monostable mode: R1 from VCC to DISCH(7)+THRESH(6), C1 from THRESH to GND, negative-going trigger on TRIG(2).

values.worked_example: R1 = 2.2 kOhm, C1 = 0.01 uF gives tW = 24.2 us (Example 7-13)

source.book: Digital Fundamentals, 11th ed., Thomas L. Floyd
source.section: 7-5 One-Shots, 'The 555 Timer as a One-Shot', Equation 7-3, Figure 7-53, Example 7-13

statement: A 555 timer in astable mode (THRESH tied to TRIG, C1 charging through R1+R2 and discharging through R2) oscillates at f = 1.44/((R1+2R2)*C1) with duty cycle (R1+R2)/(R1+2R2)*100%, which is always above 50% and approaches 50% only when R2 >> R1.
condition: 555 astable: R1 from VCC to DISCH(7), R2 from DISCH to THRESH(6)+TRIG(2), C1 from that node to GND; 0.01 uF decoupling on CONT(5).

values.duty_cycle_limit: > 50% in the basic circuit; near 50% requires R2 >> R1
values.worked_example: R1 = 2.2 kOhm, R2 = 4.7 kOhm, C1 = 0.022 uF gives f = 5.64 kHz, duty = 59.5% (Example 7-14)

source.book: Digital Fundamentals, 11th ed., Thomas L. Floyd
source.section: 7-6 The Astable Multivibrator, Equations 7-4 to 7-7, Figure 7-56, Example 7-14

statement: To get a 555 astable duty cycle below 50%, place a diode across R2 (anode toward DISCH) so C1 charges only through R1 and discharges only through R2; then duty = R1/(R1+R2)*100%, made < 50% by choosing R1 < R2.
condition: 555 astable circuit modified with diode D1 in parallel with R2 (Figure 7-59) and R1 < R2.

source.book: Digital Fundamentals, 11th ed., Thomas L. Floyd

statement: TTL fan-out in unit loads is IOL/IIL of the family, and the LOW-state sink current is the limiting factor: a 74LS gate (IOL = 8.0 mA, IIL = 0.4 mA) can drive at most 20 same-family inputs. CMOS (74HC) fan-out is not DC-limited but frequency-limited: each added input adds parallel input capacitance that lengthens charge/discharge times, so fewer loads allow higher maximum operating frequency.
condition: Gate output driving multiple gate inputs of the same logic family.

values.cmos_note: 74HC/CMOS fan-out is capacitive and frequency-dependent; no fixed DC unit-load number is given

erc_rule: For bipolar/TTL families, flag any net where the number of driven same-family inputs exceeds IOL/IIL (20 for 74LS); for CMOS-only nets, warn on high fan-out at high clock frequency instead.

source.book: Digital Fundamentals, 11th ed., Thomas L. Floyd
source.section: 3-8 Fan-Out and Loading (p.168) and 15-1 Loading and Fan-Out (pp.861-863)

statement: Never leave logic-gate inputs floating. For AND/NAND, tie unused inputs to VCC — through a 1.0 kOhm resistor for bipolar/TTL (CMOS can tie directly); for OR/NOR, tie unused inputs to ground; alternatively tie them to a used input of the same gate or to a spare gate output held at the required constant level. CMOS inputs especially must go to supply or ground because a floating CMOS input acquires electrostatic charge and floats to unpredictable levels.
condition: Any gate input pin that is not driven by a signal.

values.cmos: direct to VCC or GND, never open
values.tied_together_caveat: on TTL OR/NOR each tied-together input counts as a separate LOW-state unit load; on AND/NAND all tied inputs count as one LOW-state unit load

erc_rule: Flag any unconnected input pin on a logic IC. Accept: connection to VCC (via 1.0 kOhm for TTL AND/NAND), connection to GND (OR/NOR), or connection to another input/constant-level output.

source.book: Digital Fundamentals, 11th ed., Thomas L. Floyd
source.section: 15-4 Practical Considerations in the Use of TTL, 'Unused TTL Inputs' / 'Inputs to VCC or Ground' (p.879); CMOS rule in 15-2 (p.868); summary in 3-8 (p.169)

statement: Worst-case logic levels: 5 V CMOS — VIL(max) 1.5 V, VIH(min) 3.5 V, VOL(max) 0.33 V, VOH(min) 4.4 V; 3.3 V CMOS — VIL(max) 0.8 V, VIH(min) 2 V, VOL(max) 0.4 V, VOH(min) 2.4 V; bipolar TTL — VIL(max) 0.8 V, VIH(min) 2 V, VOL(max) 0.4 V, VOH(min) 2.4 V. Noise margins follow as VNH = VOH(min) - VIH(min) and VNL = VIL(max) - VOL(max): 0.9 V/1.17 V for 5 V CMOS, 0.4 V/0.4 V for TTL.
condition: Interfacing logic families on the same net, or computing noise margin for a driver-receiver pair.
formula: VNH = VOH(min) - VIH(min); VNL = VIL(max) - VOL(max)
erc_rule: For every cross-family driver-receiver pair require VOH(min,driver) >= VIH(min,receiver) and VOL(max,driver) <= VIL(max,receiver). This fails for a TTL output (VOH(min) = 2.4 V) driving a 5 V CMOS input (VIH(min) = 3.5 V), so flag TTL-to-5V-CMOS nets as needing a pull-up or HCT-type receiver.

source.book: Digital Fundamentals, 11th ed., Thomas L. Floyd
source.section: 15-1 Basic Operational Characteristics and Parameters, Figures 15-2/15-3, Equations 15-1/15-2, Example 15-1 (pp.856-859); same values in 3-8 (p.168)

statement: Output sink-current capability IOL by 74XX family: F 20 mA, LS 8 mA, ALS 8 mA, ABT (BiCMOS) 64 mA, HC 4 mA, AC 24 mA, AHC 8 mA, LV 12 mA, LVC 24 mA, ALVC 24 mA; gate propagation delays run F 3.3 ns, LS 10 ns, HC 7 ns, AHC 3.7 ns, LVC 4.3 ns. Use IOL when checking what a chosen family's output can drive (LEDs, terminations, mixed-family loads).
condition: Selecting a 74XX logic family or checking whether a gate output can sink the load current on its net.
erc_rule: Flag any net where total sunk current (LED + resistive + input loads) exceeds the driving family's IOL, e.g. more than 4 mA on a 74HC output.
